title: POC deployment playbook — tradeoffs and runbook
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a solutions-engineering playbook for customer POCs that compares Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment approaches and captures recommended tradeoffs, fallback patterns, and an actionable runbook for a typical 4-week customer evaluation. Intended readers: SEs running POCs, pre-sales engineering, customer infra/security reviewers, and engineering partners (infra/runtime).

Context / motivator:
We keep seeing the same decision questions during early POCs: data residency and egress, latency SLOs, throughput predictability, encryption/KMS requirements, and corporate network rules (no internet, allow only specific egress). Many customers start with Hosted for speed, then evaluate Dedicated or Private as they move toward production. This doc codifies the typical tradeoff map and gives a minimal runbook and checklist so SEs can sign customers up quickly and control risk.

High-level decision matrix (quick view):
- Hosted (fastest onboarding): +: setup < 1 hour, auto-scaling, audited models available, low SE runway; -: possible data residency/egress concerns, shared infra (logical isolation), hard to meet some enterprise SLAs. Best for: early feature validation, small-scale demos, non-sensitive data.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): +: predictable throughput/latency, SLAs, dedicated GPU pools, better isolation; -: longer lead time (days to weeks), commit-based pricing, needs capacity planning. Best for: production-bounded POCs, regulated customers wanting SLA and throughput predictability.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): +: full control over network and data, can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, air-gapped options; -: highest operational cost and setup time, requires ops coordination, possible feature parity lag. Best for: regulated industries (healthcare, finance), data residency, or corporate security policies that prohibit external API calls.

Core tradeoffs explained (SE checklist style):
1) Data path and residency
  - Hosted: data flows to Redwood cloud. Ask: Do you have contractual restrictions on sending tokens to a third party? If yes -> prefer Dedicated or Private.
  - Dedicated: possible to restrict region and limit egress; customer data still in Redwood-managed infra but logically isolated.
  - Private: data stays in customer VPC or on-prem.

2) Latency & throughput predictability
  - Hosted: good for bursty traffic; unpredictable tail latency under noisy neighbors for very strict SLOs.
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU pool, configurable autoscale/burst policies. Use for sustained throughput.
  - Private: depends on customer infra; can be optimized end-to-end but may require infra tuning.

3) Cost and procurement
  - Hosted: pay-as-you-go; minimal procurement friction.
  - Dedicated: commit-based monthly/annual; procurement conversation required.
  - Private: license/installation + ongoing support; usually enterprise contract.

4) Security and compliance
  - Hosted: SOC/ISO attestations we can present; verify SSO, RBAC, and audit log needs.
  - Dedicated: additional contractual controls available; can enable customer-managed keys (check with legal).
  - Private: integrate with KMS/HSM, custom logging, full network control.

5) Feature parity and operations
  - Hosted: latest features first.
  - Dedicated: most features, but some enterprise-only features may require config.
  - Private: some features may lag (releases scheduled); account for upgrade windows.

POC runbook (4-week template)
Week 0 — Prep (SE + Customer)
  - 2x kickoff calls (business + technical). Capture success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate) and a small evaluation dataset or prompt suite.
  - Decide target deployment mode. If undecided, default to Hosted with a migration plan to Dedicated for production.
  - Ask security questionnaire (send standard packet).

Week 1 — Fast validation (Hosted preferred)
  - Spin up hosted endpoints, curated model selection. Run baseline prompt set; capture latency and token counts.
  - Quick integration guide, sample code, and a low-friction Postman/SDK demo.
  - Record telemetries and share a first-week heatmap with the customer.

Week 2 — Scale tests and edge cases
  - Load test at expected QPS; evaluate KV-cache/prefix benefits and batching suggestions.
  - If customer requires predictability, run equivalent tests on Dedicated staging if available.
  - Capture quality/regression checks (prompt-level diffs).

Week 3 — Security/enterprise gating and cost modeling
  - Provide Dedicated / Private cost and timeline sheet. Outline KMS options and network egress plan.
  - If Private is required, begin infra runbook: VPC peer, allowed ports, cert exchange, and onboarding folder.

Week 4 — Decision and next steps
  - Final demo, executive summary (one-pager) with recommended path (hosted->dedicated or direct private).
  - If moving to Dedicated/Private, create handoff ticket to infra & account teams (include capacity plan and expected commit).

Runbook snippets and templates (copy-paste for SEs)
- Hosted quick ask to customer: "Can we use Redwood-hosted endpoints for the initial 2-week test? We'll remove any persisted data after the POC. If not, we will provide Dedicated/Private options with a technical plan."
- Security preflight checklist: SSO type, IP allowlist, KMS requirement, data classification, required attestations (SOC2/ISO), backup/ER procedures, and logging retention.

Known pitfalls and mitigation patterns
- Customer says no data leaves premise -> propose hybrid: keep pre/post-processing on-prem, call hosted endpoint with anonymized tokens OR run model on Private.
- Latency spikes on hosted during load test -> recommend Dedicated with a burst policy or model shard pinning.
- Compliance asks for certificate-level control -> Private deployment + customer-managed KMS.

Unresolved questions (to raise in infra sync):
- Exact SLA wording required by legal for Dedicated trial customers (Diego to sync with Legal).
- Minimum lead time for Dedicated capacity in APAC region — validate with Platform Eng.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: finalize host/dedicated cost template and upload to Confluence (due 2025-02-06).
- Diego: confirm Dedicated capacity lead times for APAC and EMEA (due 2025-01-20).
- Ava: create a stripped-down network onboarding checklist for Private that can be sent to customers (due 2025-01-17).
- Samir: add a sample JMeter script for sustained QPS to the poc-scripts repo (PR link in linked_artifacts).

Notes to self: keep the POC friction as low as possible — default to Hosted unless a hard security gating exists. Always attach the prompt set used for evaluation and the exact model + sampling params to the handoff ticket.

Appendix: mini FAQ for customers
Q: "Why not just start Private?" A: It's usually slower and more expensive. Start Hosted to validate the feature, then migrate if needed.
Q: "What if we need no-evidence of PII leaving our network?" A: We'll propose anonymization or Private deployment; capture exact requirements in writing.

End of doc — living playbook. Update after each major POC (label with customer name/date).
